q1: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2: WITH NOTRED AS ( SELECT COM_ID FROM COMPANY WHERE NAME ='RED' ), GETSALESID AS ( SELECT DISTINCT O.SALES_ID FROM ORDERS O, NOTRED N WHERE O.COM_ID = N.COM_ID ) SELECT S.NAME FROM SALESPERSON S WHERE S.SALES_ID NOT IN (SELECT SALES_ID FROM GETSALESID)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2_prompt_sql: WITH NOTRED AS ( SELECT COM_ID FROM COMPANY WHERE NAME ='RED' ), GETSALESID AS ( SELECT DISTINCT O.SALES_ID FROM ORDERS O, NOTRED N WHERE O.COM_ID = N.COM_ID ) SELECT S.NAME FROM SALESPERSON S WHERE S.SALES_ID NOT IN (SELECT SALES_ID FROM GETSALESID)
explanation: Both queries aim to find the names of salespersons who have not sold anything to the company named 'RED'. They achieve this by identifying salespersons who have no orders associated with the 'RED' company.
